title: Fisher information as a named curvature
dek: I(θ)=E[−ℓ̈]. Wikipedia information node. Delta method and MLE variance already have Simplfy plates.
story: Fisher information on Wikipedia is expected curvature of the log-likelihood, or equivalently the variance of the score. It is the object that turns a regular MLE into an approximate Normal with variance I(θ)⁻¹/n in iid models.
stats-fisher-information already does the TB-lab version. stats-delta-method pushes it through g(θ). This card is the encyclopedia name.
Observed information −ℓ̈(θ̂) is a cousin you actually compute; expected information is the expectation. Score tests use I at the null; Wald often uses I at the MLE.
deep: Misspecification: I is the wrong curvature; sandwich uses meat and bread (stats-sandwich).
Singular I means the parameter is locally unidentified — not a software NaN mystery.
Cramér–Rao uses I as a bound (wiki-cramer-rao).

visual.caption: More information, tighter sampling law of the MLE (schematic). Information is curvature, not a p-value.

example.title: Bernoulli π near 0, n=40
example.setup: Information I=n/(π(1−π)) is large? Wait, for π tiny, π(1−π)≈π, I≈n/π which is large per unit π, but the count is Poisson-like rare.

steps.title: Rare events: few 1s, the effective information for log-odds can still be small
Do not quote 1/I as a CI on the probability scale without looking at zeros

example.takeaway: Fisher information is curvature. Rare events can still be weakly identified on the scale you care about.

choices: Expected curvature of ℓ (variance of the score)
check.answer: Expected curvature of ℓ (variance of the score)
